price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict winning beyond team quality?
Is the recommendation derived independently of the outcome being predicted?
Is n=54 series enough for a useful test?
Is adherence measurable given tagger floors on some play types?
Is the effect distinguishable from a placebo mix or from a mechanical correlate of efficiency?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 (inflated n, team-quality confound). Series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 at n=50, underpowered, with about 80 series stated as needed for p<0.05. The low AVOID-share bin won 52.6% vs 37.0% for the 25-50% bin. Still confounded by team quality (OKC disciplined and good). Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Conformance of observed mix to the recommended opener in 4 playoff G1s (8 sides): average |delta| 4.5 to 24.0pp on leverage buckets, and 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. CUT and PNR were muted by the tagger floor. Single-game horizon, no outcome comparison. Descriptive only.

LLM counter selection vs deterministic BEST tier: n=3 triggers, agreed with BEST 1/3, picked AVOID 2/3. Mean H2 PPP was BEST 1.650, agent 1.154, AVOID 0.642. The record's caveat says 230+ disagreements are needed. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Audit of an LLM batch claiming 'adaptation predicts series winners 9/10'. Series winners were never looked up (0/2073 calls) and were LLM-inferred, one game score was invented, and 706 findings had n<5. The apparent effect came from construction flaws.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share vs winning at n=50, with a game-level version
failed_approaches.why: LIM:small_sample and LIM:confounding. The series test was underpowered (p=0.07), and the game-level test had inflated n and a team-quality confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing LLM vs BEST-tier counter selection on 3 triggers
LLM-inferred series outcomes used to claim adaptation predicts winning
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact. Outcomes were not looked up, and the finding rested on inference stacked on inference with tiny n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Conformance measured in single games with no outcome link
failed_approaches.why: E_unclear / RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR. The tagger floor muted CUT and PNR, so measured conformance is distorted for those types.

evidence_establishes: The closest prior test (FAM:SF-CHT-039, AVOID share vs winning) found a negative association in the hypothesised direction. It was not significant at series level (rho=-0.26, p=0.07, n=50) and was confounded by team quality.
The project's own record states that about 80 series are needed for p<0.05 at that effect size.
Game-level associations in this domain are inflated by non-independence and team-quality confounding.
Adherence measurement is affected by the tagger floor for some play types (FAM:SF-APPS-017).
Outcome labels such as series winners must be taken from the data, not inferred (FAM:SF-APPA-008).
evidence_does_not_establish: That adherence predicts winning once team quality is controlled.
Any outcome-linked test of the full recommended mix, as opposed to AVOID share alone.
That the BEST tier outperforms AVOID or alternatives beyond tiny samples (n=3).
Whether the recommendation engine is calibrated out of sample.
own_inferences: With n=54, a true rho of about -0.26 gives a two-sided p near 0.06 and power of roughly 45%. A series-level test as posed is likely to be inconclusive again, even if the effect is real.
Strong teams plausibly both adhere more (disciplined, better execution) and win more, so an unadjusted association is expected under the null.

The recommended mix is probably computed from the same games and play-type efficiencies that define winning, so there is a risk of outcome-derived or look-ahead labels unless it is rebuilt out of sample.
Nesting the 54 series within 4 seasons and repeated teams reduces the effective sample size.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-06-16, so any series counted from them may be incomplete or have unknown winners until 2026-06-21.
uncertainties: How adherence is defined (distance metric, leverage weighting, handling of suppression triggers) is not recorded for this question.
It is unknown whether the current 54 series include incomplete 2025-26 playoff series.
It is unknown whether the recommended mix is computed ex ante from prior data or from the same game.
It is not recorded whether FAM:SF-CHT-039 used the same recommendation engine version.
No validation was recorded for any retrieved family.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history, a straightforward series-level correlation might have been run. FAM:SF-CHT-039 shows that this exact design already ended inconclusive from low power and confounding, and that n=54 is still short of the roughly 80 stated as needed. FAM:SF-APPA-008 shows that outcome labels must be sourced rather than inferred. So the decision moved from 'proceed' to 'proceed with changes': use game-level data with series clustering and team-quality adjustment, and treat the 54-series test as secondary.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives about 45% power for the rho of roughly -0.26 seen previously. The project's own record puts the need at about 80 series.
Team quality drives both adherence and winning. A series-level test needs a pre-series strength covariate that is not derived from the same games.
The recommended mix must be built only from data preceding each game or series. Otherwise adherence is partly a function of the outcome.

prior_work.summary: The AVOID-share version was tested and left inconclusive: the direction was negative but p=0.07 at n=50, and the result was confounded by team quality. Full-mix adherence has no outcome-linked test. Other records are descriptive, tiny-n or artifactual, so none answers the question.

risks.text: The series-level test is underpowered at n=54, so a null cannot be read as no effect.
Team quality, opponent strength, home court and injuries affect both adherence and winning.
The recommended mix and the suppression trigger may be derived from the same outcomes (efficiency) used to define success.
The recommendation must use only information available before the games it is scored on, not full-series or full-season efficiencies.
The tagger floor mutes CUT and PNR, which distorts adherence for those play types.
Adherence over about 100 possessions per game is noisy, and its definition varies with leverage weighting.
Teams are selected on a suppression trigger that is likely followed by reversion to normal efficiency, which can mimic a benefit.
There are several possible adherence metrics, tiers, lags and subsets, so a forking-paths risk applies.
Series winners and scores must be taken from the box score or graph, as FAM:SF-APPA-008 showed inferred winners were wrong.
Engine, tagging and league style may differ across the four seasons, and 2025-26 playoff data are partial before 2026-06-21.

design.estimand: Within-series, game-level association between a team's pre-registered adherence score (leverage-weighted distance to the ex ante suppression-conditional recommended mix) and winning that game, adjusted for pre-game team strength. Secondary: the series-level association between mean adherence and series win.
design.unit: Team-game after a suppression trigger (primary), clustered by series. Series (secondary).
design.sample: All completed series in 2022-23 to 2025-26, with 2025-26 playoff series included only once complete (on or after 2026-06-21). Winners come from box-score or graph lookup. Freeze the series list and engine version before looking at outcomes.
design.power: The series-level secondary test at n=54 has about 45% power for rho=-0.26 and is reported as exploratory, not confirmatory. The primary test uses game-level data with series-clustered or mixed-effects standard errors. A minimum detectable effect is computed from the effective (cluster-adjusted) sample size before analysis. If that effect is implausibly large, the study is declared underpowered and stops short of a confirmatory claim.
design.controls: Pre-series strength (prior-season net rating or an ex ante rating not using the test games), opponent strength, home court, rest, and series game number. Rebuild the recommended mix leave-one-series-out or only from prior seasons or prior games. Use the score deficit and leverage at trigger time. Report adherence by play type with and without CUT and PNR to expose the tagger-floor effect.
design.falsification: Placebo recommended mixes (shuffled tiers, random mix with the same marginals, the opponent's recommendation) should show no association. A permutation test of adherence labels within series is run. The association should vanish or shrink once team-quality controls are added if it is purely talent. Negative-control outcome: adherence after the game result is known should not be treated as predictive.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis: a negative coefficient on distance-to-recommendation (equivalently, positive on adherence) at game level. The adherence metric, lag and covariates are fixed in advance. All secondary and subset analyses are labelled exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary coefficient has the predicted sign, the cluster-robust two-sided p<0.05 holds after strength controls, and the placebo mixes fail to match it. Rejected only if the 95% CI excludes the minimum effect of interest, which is possible only when the power check passes. Otherwise report inconclusive and say how many series would be needed (about 80 or more for the series-level test). Any effect that disappears under strength controls is recorded as talent confounding.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type graph, seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26. The 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13. The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-06-16 and complete from 2026-06-21. Freeze the snapshot date, tagger version and engine version at registration.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict winning at the series or game level?
How is the recommended mix derived and is it independent of the outcome (leakage, outcome-derived labels)?
Is there sufficient exposure and sample size with 54 series?
How to control for confounding by team quality and opponent, and regression to the mean?
Is the effect distinguishable from a mechanical floor or placebo mix?
args.query: adherence to suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix predicts winning; best/avoid counter strategy against defensive suppression; series-level test

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I could pull in a follow-up tool, but I think I can finish without it. I'm weighing whether to read FAM:SF-CHT-039 for more detail, though I'll keep things efficient. The series count is now 54 rather than the 50 I noted earlier, and I need roughly 80 series for the power I want. The 2025-26 playoffs only finish on 2026-06-21, and the question was posed on 2026-06-16, so that data is still partial.

I'm drafting the JSON output now. The series count of 54 gives about 45% power for a true correlation of -0.26 at p≈0.057, which is underpowered, so I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes: switch to game-level analysis clustered by series and adjusted for team strength, with the series-level check kept as a secondary confirmatory test.
